method: Classify all mutually exclusive Studio-reported attribution rows in one channel and observation window before computing shares. A risk index is a descriptive diagnostic, not observed income risk.

source_families.label: Browse
source_families.source: YouTube Home, Subscriptions, Watch Later, Explore and other browse surfaces

source_families.label: Suggested videos
source_families.source: Recommendations adjacent to or after videos and links in descriptions

source_families.label: Notifications
source_families.source: Notification/email referrals; subscriber notifications are not the subscriber count

source_families.label: Playlists
source_families.source: Creator or other curated playlists, including liked/favorite videos

source_families.label: External
source_families.source: Links/embeds from external websites or applications

source_families.label: Direct or unknown
source_families.source: Bookmarks, direct URLs, signed-out viewers and unidentified apps

source_families.label: Other Studio source classes
source_families.source: Remaining channel pages, cards, remixes, sound pages, ads and product placements when reported

descriptive_indices.formula: largest reported source view count / total attributed views
descriptive_indices.interpretation: Share attributed to largest distinct reported source; do not infer independent control of that source.

descriptive_indices.formula: sum of squared fractions across all disjoint reported source categories
descriptive_indices.interpretation: Descriptive source concentration; different taxonomy granularity changes its value.
Only a mathematical equivalent, not the number of algorithms or independently owned audience paths.

risk_conditions: Owner-only Studio rows cannot establish competitor source concentration.
Browse features mix Home and subscriptions; do not label entire browse category algorithmic recommendation.
Suggested videos can include description links; do not treat the category as exclusively automated suggestions.
Direct/unknown can include signed-out viewers and unidentified apps; do not declare those independently owned or a deliberate direct audience.
Shares of views are not shares of revenue, watch time, unique people, sponsor conversions or net profit.
Include reported paid promotions and all traffic source classes rather than excluding inconvenient categories to raise or lower a share.
Shorts and long-form viewer sources and the 2026 view definition revision require separate windows/format-specific analysis.
HHI depends on the partition's detail level; no universal safe threshold or creator success probability is established.

research_gates.reason: No channel owner data supplied or collected
Complete counts and explicit zero rows are not available
A consistent channel/metric/format window has not been measured
No joint revenue, disruptions, retention or causal outcomes measured

categories.meaning: Website link outside YouTube, including Google Search referrals
categories.limits: Google Search traffic is external, not YT_SEARCH.

categories.meaning: An embedded video on another website
categories.limits: Embedding does not prove visitor ownership or portable account contacts.

categories.meaning: No identified referrer, including direct links and mobile app traffic
categories.limits: Direct/unknown cannot be relabeled loyal users or subscriber acquisitions.

categories.meaning: A related-video listing on another video's watch page
categories.limits: Suggested Studio reporting can also include certain video-description links; no public causal algorithm weights.

categories.meaning: A vertical swipe from a previous Short in Shorts viewing
categories.limits: This traffic-source code is not the same as creatorContentType=SHORTS or raw Shorts play starts.
Distinct from Google Search, which may appear under EXT_URL.
Referral source does not establish viewer subscribedStatus at event time.

categories.meaning: A YouTube notification or email alert
categories.limits: A notification-origin visit is not a unique subscriber or guaranteed opted-in contact.
Track separately from organic referral; paid viewers are not earned subscribers or creator income.

categories.meaning: A video was played from a playlist
categories.limits: Includes playlist contexts that may be owned by another channel.

categories.meaning: Video watched or reached from channel page
categories.limits: Channel page views may originate from owner or unrelated channel pages.
Generic source, not necessarily organic algorithmic exposure.

categories.meaning: A remix player's link to the original
categories.limits: A remix referral is not an automatically licensed commercial derivative.
Audio page source is different from a Shorts-feed swipe.

categories.meaning: Link from another video's end screen
categories.limits: No inference about paid partnerships or cross-channel audience identity.

semantic_boundaries: YouTube Search (YT_SEARCH) and Google Search external links (EXT_URL) are different acquisition families.
API SUBSCRIBER is a referral type for homepage/subscriptions and is not subscribedStatus (SUBSCRIBED or UNSUBSCRIBED), creator subscriber count, or an owner-controlled export.
API SHORTS as traffic origin is different from content format creatorContentType=SHORTS; the vertical feed is also distinct from sound pages and remix referral.
NO_LINK_OTHER does not establish a direct loyal subscriber or a source entirely controlled by a creator.
Source-type splits require owner authorization and compatible date, content format, metric, geography, and category completeness; source-detail reports may show only top referring terms or pages.
A video may be found from outside websites by search engines without the viewer ever entering YouTube native search.
Referral view counts cannot infer unique people, actual click-through without matched impressions, paid media costs, net income, or niche competition.
YouTube's August 24, 2026 view-count revision requires a metric-definition boundary for historical comparisons.
